request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: Run 2 (RF, all) has PR-AUC 0.7355 vs logistic 0.6809, a gain of 0.0546 that is slightly below one SD (~0.06), so by the stated rule the simpler logistic (run 1) is technically preferred; however logistic uses no_size features, so the comparison is confounded by feature set.
Run 3 LightGBM (0.7353) is statistically indistinguishable from RF (0.7355); added complexity and agent features give no benefit. Run 4 is worse and has the highest SD.
All differences among runs 2-4 are well within fold noise (SD ~0.06), so ranking among them is not meaningful and further tuning is unlikely to help.

ROC-AUC of ~0.94 and PR-AUC ~0.7 at 9.35% prevalence is high; the label origin is undocumented and may be derived from or correlated with claim-level patterns, so the model may be learning to reproduce the labeling rule rather than detect fraud.
Provider size features (in 'all') may act as proxies for volume; the no_size logistic still scores 0.68, suggesting signal is not just size, but size-dependent leakage cannot be excluded.
Claims span about 13 months; no temporal split is evident, so fold estimates may be optimistic if random CV was used. Provider-level folds are assumed, not confirmed.
Precision@50 of 0.74-0.78 is on the 100-provider queue scale only partially; k=100 was not reported.
Choosing run 2 over run 1 is a judgment call: the gain is near but under 1 SD, and the models differ in feature set. If strict simplicity is required, run 1 is the fallback.
